title: Srrm2 depletion is tolerated in several cortical classes but drives abundance programs in thalamic, midbrain, and related GABAergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Acute Srrm2 depletion produced a highly cell-state-selective abundance phenotype in which thalamic, midbrain, and related GABAergic classes carried most corrected downstream responses, while several cortical and Pvalb classes reduced Srrm2 without corrected off-target genes. / Multiple FDR-supported perturbations in RNA-processing factors or Huwe1 produced nonuniform neuronal signatures centered on Srrm2, Srsf-family, Rsrp1, Tcea2, Pabpn1, and related spliceosome or nuclear-speckle transcripts, with thalamic and midbrain classes repeatedly carrying the broadest response while other target-shifted classes were buffered.
biological_interpretation: The nuclear-speckle factor SRRM2 is a loss-of-function vulnerability for a subset of thalamic/midbrain neuronal states rather than a universal neuronal transcript-abundance dependency. / Selected subcortical neurons are acutely sensitive to partial nuclear-speckle or spliceosome stress, so local SR-factor/nuclear-speckle marker panels should be better pharmacodynamic and liability readouts than the target-RNA row alone.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

support.evidence_summary: Srrm2:F001/F002 and the Nop56/Huwe1/Tnpo3/Snrnp70/U2af2 F001 findings resolve overlapping but distinct cell-selective nuclear-speckle and RNA-processing signatures.

caveats: The story spans several distinct RNA-processing factors and should not be read as direct epistasis.
Some U2af2 and Tnpo3 response classes lack FDR-significant self-mRNA loss.

prior_expectation.summary: Srrm2:F001/F002 and the Nop56/Huwe1/Tnpo3/Snrnp70/U2af2 F001 findings resolve overlapping but distinct cell-selective nuclear-speckle and RNA-processing signatures.
